chunk_findings.detail: `wt = Path(out.data["worktree"])` treats the worktree path as absolute or relative to the current process cwd, not relative to `repo`. The incident itself shows worktrees are represented as repo-relative paths like `.ddflow/worktrees/B95-false-limit`. When pytest runs with cwd != `repo` (the normal `tmp_path` fixture case), `(wt / rel)` and `_git("-C", str(wt), ...)` target a directory under the wrong repository, so `_git` raises `CalledProcessError: not a git repository` before either test reaches its assertions. The path should be `Path(repo) / out.data["worktree"]`.

chunk_findings.detail: When the author has no prior session record (`own` is empty, so `current` is None), the code still calls `sessions.start(log, cfg, model=model, session_id="")`, which starts a brand-new, never-ended session. That is exactly the state the updated docstring says this change must avoid: a fresh open session re-points the lanes ledger's `session`/`ended` signal and makes a finished lane read as still open. The new regression test only seeds an existing ended session, so it does not exercise this `current is None` branch and would pass even though the no-session case remains broken.
